---
title: "Solution: Loss Functions — RMSE and MAE"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
```

```{r sample-data}
set.seed(42)
d100 <- diamonds |> slice_sample(n = 100)
```

## Task 1: Implement RMSE and MAE

```{r task1}
rmse_fn <- function(b0, b1, data) {
  pred  <- b0 + b1 * data$carat
  resid <- data$price - pred
  sqrt(mean(resid^2))
}

mae_fn <- function(b0, b1, data) {
  pred  <- b0 + b1 * data$carat
  resid <- data$price - pred
  mean(abs(resid))
}
```

## Task 2: Evaluate at a candidate parameter pair

```{r task2}
cat("RMSE at (-2000, 7000):", round(rmse_fn(-2000, 7000, d100), 2), "\n")
cat("MAE  at (-2000, 7000):", round(mae_fn( -2000, 7000, d100), 2), "\n")

# RMSE >= MAE always holds because squaring amplifies large residuals.
# The gap between them indicates the presence of some large errors
# (diamonds whose price is far from the linear prediction).
```

## Task 3: Random search over 250 parameter pairs

```{r task3}
set.seed(7)
search <- tibble(
  b0 = runif(250, -5000, 0),
  b1 = runif(250,  5000, 12000)
) |>
  mutate(rmse = map2_dbl(b0, b1, rmse_fn, data = d100))

head(search)
```

## Task 4: Report the best pair

```{r task4}
best_random <- search |> slice_min(rmse, n = 1)
print(best_random)

# Compare to the OLS solution for reference
ols_mod <- lm(price ~ carat, data = d100)
ols_rmse <- sqrt(mean(residuals(ols_mod)^2))
cat("OLS RMSE:", round(ols_rmse, 2), "\n")
cat("Random search best RMSE:", round(best_random$rmse, 2), "\n")
# OLS always wins — it uses the mathematical optimum, not random luck.
```

## Task 5: Heatmap of the loss surface

```{r task5}
ggplot(search, aes(x = b0, y = b1, colour = rmse)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "RMSE") +
  labs(
    title    = "RMSE over the (b0, b1) parameter space — 250 random samples",
    subtitle = "Low RMSE (dark) forms a narrow valley. OLS finds the exact minimum.",
    x        = expression(beta[0] ~ "(intercept)"),
    y        = expression(beta[1] ~ "(slope)")
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Interpretation: The low-RMSE region (dark purple) forms a curved valley
# running diagonally across the parameter space. Many combinations of b0
# and b1 give similar RMSE — this is because the two parameters are
# correlated. OLS analytically finds the exact bottom of this valley.
```
